claim: Over HTTP/2 on TCP, a lost or reordered packet stalls all active transactions, even those not directly affected by it.
quote: a lost or reordered packet causes all active transactions to experience a stall regardless of whether that transaction was directly impacted by the lost packet.

claim: The reason HTTP/2 stalls on packet loss is that TCP's loss recovery cannot see the parallel nature of HTTP/2 multiplexing.
quote: because the parallel nature of HTTP/2's multiplexing is not visible to TCP's loss recovery mechanisms

claim: In HTTP/3, streams are independent, so a loss on one stream does not prevent progress on other streams.
quote: Streams are independent of each other, so one stream that is blocked or suffers packet loss does not prevent progress on other streams.

claim: QUIC avoids head-of-line blocking across multiple streams.
quote: One of the benefits of QUIC is avoidance of head-of-line blocking across multiple streams.

claim: When a packet is lost, only the streams with data in that packet are blocked waiting for retransmission; other streams continue.
quote: When a packet loss occurs, only streams with data in that packet are blocked waiting for a retransmission to be received

claim: Head-of-line blocking across streams can still occur in QUIC when one packet carries data from several streams, since losing that packet blocks all of them.
quote: Note that when data from multiple streams is included in a single QUIC packet, loss of that packet blocks all those streams from making progress.

claim: QUIC's PTO includes the peer's maximum expected acknowledgment delay instead of a fixed minimum timeout.
quote: QUIC's PTO includes the peer's maximum expected acknowledgment delay instead of using a fixed minimum timeout.

claim: The PTO is computed from the smoothed RTT, the RTT variance, and max_ack_delay.
quote: PTO = smoothed_rtt + max(4*rttvar, kGranularity) + max_ack_delay

claim: In QUIC, a PTO timer expiration does not indicate packet loss and must not cause unacknowledged packets to be marked lost.
quote: A PTO timer expiration event does not indicate packet loss and MUST NOT cause prior unacknowledged packets to be marked as lost.

claim: QUIC does not collapse the congestion window when the PTO expires, because a single tail packet loss does not indicate persistent congestion.
quote: QUIC does not collapse the congestion window when the PTO expires, since a single packet loss at the tail does not indicate persistent congestion.

claim: The recommended initial packet reordering threshold (kPacketThreshold) is 3.
quote: The RECOMMENDED initial value for the packet reordering threshold (kPacketThreshold) is 3

claim: A packet is declared lost if it was sent kPacketThreshold packets before an acknowledged packet.
quote: The packet was sent kPacketThreshold packets before an acknowledged packet

claim: The PTO allows a connection to recover from loss of tail packets or acknowledgments.
quote: A PTO enables a connection to recover from loss of tail packets or acknowledgments.

claim: QUIC's handshake can allow a client to send application data immediately (0-RTT), but this requires prior communication or configuration.
quote: This includes an option for clients to send data immediately (0-RTT), which requires some form of prior communication or configuration to enable.

claim: 0-RTT data gives no protection against replay attacks.
quote: However, 0-RTT provides no protection against replay attacks

claim: Packets that are not ack-eliciting are acknowledged only when an ACK frame is sent for other reasons.
quote: Packets that are not ack-eliciting are only acknowledged when an ACK frame is sent for other reasons.

claim: HTTP/2 does not address TCP head-of-line blocking.
quote: Note, however, that TCP head-of-line blocking is not addressed by this protocol.

claim: QUIC incorporates stream multiplexing and per-stream flow control, similar to the HTTP/2 framing layer.
quote: The QUIC transport protocol incorporates stream multiplexing and per-stream flow control, similar to that provided by the HTTP/2 framing layer.

claim: The IMC 2017 study reports that QUIC generally outperforms TCP.
quote: QUIC generally outperforms TCP, but we also identified

quote: QUIC’s performance diminishes on mobile devices and over cellular networks.

claim: In the IMC 2017 study's desktop environment, QUIC outperformed TCP+HTTPS in nearly every scenario.
quote: In the desktop environment, QUIC outperforms TCP+HTTPS in nearly every scenario.

claim: The IMC 2017 study found that a TCP proxy can narrow TCP's gap with QUIC under packet loss, and in low-latency cases.
quote: A TCP proxy can help TCP to shrink the performance gap with QUIC in low latency cases and also under loss.

claim: The IMC 2017 study found that QUIC performs significantly worse than TCP in many scenarios when packets are re-ordered.
quote: In presence of packet re-ordering, QUIC performs significantly worse than TCP in many scenarios.

claim: The IMC 2017 study found that all of QUIC's performance gains are diminished on phones from 2013 and late 2014.
quote: all of QUIC’s performance gains are diminished on phones from 2013 and late 2014.

claim: Yu and Benson (WWW 2021) found that QUIC's removal of head-of-line blocking had little impact on Page Load Time and Speed Index relative to congestion control for real-world web pages.
quote: QUIC’s removal of HOL (head-of-line) blocking has little impact on Page Load Time and Speed Index relative to congestion control for real-world web-pages.

claim: Yu and Benson (WWW 2021) report that overall QUIC performance is largely determined by the server's choice of congestion-control algorithm.
quote: its overall performance is largely determined by the server’s choice of congestion-control algorithm

claim: In Yu and Benson's 1% added-loss tests, HTTP/3 performed much worse than HTTP/2 against the Cloudflare endpoint.
quote: Cloudflare is the only exception to this pattern, where H3 performed much worse than H2 during 1% added loss.

claim: Yu and Benson report that QUIC's 1-RTT handshake advantage has a significant impact on connections whose payload is less than 1MB, but negligible impact otherwise.
quote: QUIC’s 1 RTT advantage has a significant impact on connections whose payload is less than 1MB, but negligible impact otherwise.

claim: Yu and Benson's Cloudflare analysis found that congestion-control reaction to loss affects time to last byte far more than the total number of lost packets.
quote: demonstrating how the congestion control’s reaction to loss affects TTLB far more than the total number of lost packets.

claim: Wolsing et al. (ANRW 2019) report that in lossy networks QUIC clearly outperforms the current web stack.
quote: In lossy networks, QUIC clearly outperforms the current Web stack

claim: Wolsing et al. (ANRW 2019) found that the choice of congestion control has an immense impact, especially in lossy environments.
quote: Our study further highlights the immense impact of choice of congestion control, especially in lossy environments.

claim: Wolsing et al. (ANRW 2019) found that tuning TCP closes the gap to QUIC, leaving TCP still very competitive.
